title: Teach Me Something New
heading: Part II. Novel
keyClaims: Chapter 4 argues that audiences lean toward novelty and pay more attention when a talk teaches them something new or reframes something familiar in a fresh way.
Ballard, Cameron, and Rosling are used to show that discovery and unexpected framing can make even technical material feel engaging.
Novelty fails when it collapses into cliché, exhausted solutions, or cleverness that does not help the audience learn.

usedFor: teach one new useful thing rule
